subject: Sentinel standup: FluentAI latency & error surge — customer status + leadership asks
messages:
From: Carlos Jordan <c.jordan@fluentai.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com
Cc: infra@fluentai.com, sara.lee@enterpriseops.io
Date: 2026-12-18T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden error-rate spike & tail latency increase (production)

Hi Michael —

We started seeing a rise in 5xx errors and tail latency across our inference routes this morning (09:00 PST). Impact: ~18% request failures, 500ms+ p95 to p99 tail latency on the /generate endpoint. This is affecting our customer-facing chat feature; users are seeing delays or failures.

Quick data we pulled: attached is a short CSV with request counts and error rates by minute (fluentai_sla_metrics_q4.csv). Also attaching representative error traces (fluentai_error_samples.txt).

Our SRE tried scaling replicas but errors persisted. Can Redwood confirm whether this looks like a model-serving regression, routing overload, or something on the infra side? We have a contract SLA; this is high priority for our ops and PMs.

Can we get a war-room and an ETA for root cause?

— Carlos
Director, Platform Engineering
FluentAI
From: michael_grant@redwood.com
To: Carlos Jordan <c.jordan@fluentai.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden error-rate spike & tail latency increase (production)

Carlos — thanks for the data and the sample traces. We're standing up a focused response now. Immediate plan:

- 10:00 PST war-room (Zoom) — invite sent to SRE + Eng + Customer Ops.
- Triage owners: Grace (serving/runtime), Aditya (deploy/traffic routing), Monica (CS/comm).
- Initial asks for FluentAI: correlation id for a replay window (08:30–09:30 PST) and any synthetic requests you can share.

What we will do in the first 30m: collect per-host p95/p99, current queue/backlog, recent model variant rollouts, and whether any auto-scaling events or kernel changes occurred. If we need executive attention, I'll escalate after the first checkpoint (10:30 PST).

Attaching a short mitigation runbook we've used in similar incidents: mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf.

— Michael
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden error-rate spike & tail latency increase (production) — telemetry snapshot

War-room notes (first 30m):

Summary: We observed a simultaneous increase in KV cache thrashing and model loading errors (OOMs) on a subset of dedicated serving nodes behind the FluentAI route. A recent background rollout of a quantized variant to reduce cost appears to have triggered higher memory churn under FluentAI's typical long-sequence workload. Key observations:

- p95/p99 increased as batch sizes fluctuated; p50 mostly unchanged.
- OOMs correlate with nodes running model: redwood/v2q-3b-quant (rolled 12/17 22:00 UTC).
- Autoscaler briefly spun new pods but they failed health checks and were removed.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:15–10:45 PST):
- Blocked rollout to FluentAI traffic and pinned to last stable variant (redwood/v2-3b).
- Increased per-node memory reserve and disabled the memory-optimizing kernel path for the affected model variant.
- Deployed a temporary traffic-shedding rule for non-critical endpoints to keep core flows within p99 SLO.

Next steps:
1) Re-run acceptance tests with FluentAI sample sequences (Aditya).
2) Run a controlled canary of the quantized variant with reduced concurrency and modified batch budgets (Grace).
3) Prepare an incident summary for execs if errors don't fall below 2% within 2 hours (Michael).

Logs and traces saved to the incident folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1k_mitigation_runbook (see /telemetry/snapshots/2026-12-18-10-00).

— Grace
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Jordan <c.jordan@fluentai.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden error-rate spike & tail latency increase (production) — confirmation

Thanks — I can confirm the sample sequences are available and we've queued a replay window for 10:30–11:00 PST. Our PMs will standby while you run the acceptance tests. Two asks from our side:

- Please prioritize the primary /generate route for FluentAI (we will accept throttling on low-priority analytics endpoints).
- Keep us updated on whether the rollback to redwood/v2-3b will be persistent or temporary (we need to know if we should toggle our client-side fallbacks).

We'll be on the Zoom.

— Carlos
From: michael_grant@redwood.com
To: leadership@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-20T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Executive snapshot — FluentAI priority escalation (status & asks)

Leaders — brief update and requested decisions. Condensed timeline:

- 2026-12-18 09:00 PST: FluentAI reports ~18% 5xx rate + p99 tail latency spikes.
- 2026-12-18 10:15 PST: We pinned traffic away from the quantized rollout, applied memory reserves, and traffic shedding. Error rate dropped from 18% to ~3% over 90 minutes.
- 2026-12-19: Controlled canary run executed; results show memory churn persists at higher sequence lengths under the quantized kernel.
- 2026-12-20 16:00 PST: Engineering recommends disabling the quantized kernel for production rollouts of redwood/v2q-3b until a kernel patch (RW-KRN-442) is backported and validated.

Current status: FluentAI production routes are stable at ~1.7% error rate and p99 within their SLA for most traffic. The canary is paused.

Decisions / asks for leadership:
1) Approve an accelerated backport and high-priority QA cycle for RW-KRN-442 (expected 3 business days vs standard 10). This will require engineering to reassign two senior kernel engineers and pause a non-critical feature branch.
2) Approve a one-time operational credit concession to FluentAI for the four-hour outage window (proposed credit: 10% of Dec usage) to preserve the account relationship. Pricing & finance input: Monica, please advise.

Risk if we do nothing: longer-term customer impact and potential churn; risk to brand for enterprise references.

Attachments: incident telemetry + proposed credit worksheet (fluentai_sla_metrics_q4.csv, mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf).

I'll hold a short sync tomorrow 09:30 PST if leadership wants an exec-level walkthrough.

— Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
